metadataDecisions.rationale: Figure 7 is a 21-panel Wikimedia correlation composite (credit: DenisBoigelot) plotting thousands of points per panel. It cannot be reproduced as accessible inline SVG under the no-file-backed-images rule, and it has no formula to render from. It is replaced by eight panels built from explicit point sets recorded in each figure's data-spec, spanning the same pedagogical range: r = 1 and r = -1 drawn exactly from y = 0.8x + 1 and y = 9 - 0.8x; r = 0.8, 0.4, 0.0, -0.4, -0.8 generated as y = 5 + 1.9(rho*z_x + sqrt(1-rho^2)*z_e) with z_e orthogonal to z_x, rounded to 0.1, and verified at r = 0.8065, 0.4009, 0.0082, -0.3908, -0.7984; and a nonlinear r = 0 panel from y = 8 - 0.28(x-5)^2 with symmetric jitter. The Wikimedia credit is retained in the attribution footer, which also discloses the substitution. This is a deliberate local replacement, not a transcription of the source figure: do not reverse it toward the composite in a later audit.

Two Try It exercises are revalued, not rewritten. Upstream evaluates $-\tfrac12 - y$ at $y = -\tfrac14$, whose answer $-\tfrac14$ is the substituted value itself — a fixed point — and $3ab^2$ at $a = -\tfrac23, b = -\tfrac12$, whose answer $-\tfrac12$ is the substituted $b$. In both, a learner who reads the printed substitution back into the box is graded correct without evaluating anything, and the replay gate (npm run verify:replay) fails the exercise for exactly that reason. The substituted values move to $y = -\tfrac34$ (answer $\tfrac14$) and $b = -\tfrac13$ (answer $-\tfrac29$); the expressions, the method, and the arithmetic difficulty are unchanged, and no printed span of either new prompt grades correct. Deliberate local revaluation: do not reverse it toward the upstream numbers in a later audit.

sourceItems: Try It: determine whether an ordered pair is a solution of a system
metadataDecisions.rationale: One authored sub-exercise is revalued. It substituted $(0,0)$ into $x + 2y$ for the system $3x + y = 0, x + 2y = -5$, where the point satisfies the first equation but not the second — the pedagogical point — but the answer $0$ is also the substituted value, so a learner reading $x = 0$ off the prompt is graded correct, and the zero also hides the arithmetic behind the multiply-by-zero shortcut. The substitution moves to $(2,-6)$, which has the identical property (it satisfies $3x + y = 0$ and gives $-10 \ne -5$) and requires the multiplication and addition to be carried out. Deliberate local revaluation: do not reverse it toward $(0,0)$ in a later audit.

metadataDecisions.rationale: The fluorochrome example sentence says Texas red is excited by blue light and FITC absorbs invisible ultraviolet light. Manufacturer spectral data (Thermo Fisher Molecular Probes Handbook: Texas Red sulfonyl chloride absorption 588 nm; fluorescein/FITC peak excitation 488-495 nm) place Texas red's excitation in the orange and FITC's in the visible blue. The local sentence states orange and blue, carries a visible Source note, and the footer discloses the change. Found by the prose claim pass, September 6, 2026.

The source dates the Athenian plague 'between 430 and 410 BC'. Thucydides describes the outbreak of 430 BC and its recurrence ending in 426 BC, and the modern review (Littman, Mount Sinai Journal of Medicine 76 [2009]: 456-467, doi:10.1002/msj.20137) dates it 430-426 BC; no source supports 410. The local page prints 426 BC with a visible Source note and footer disclosure. Found by the prose claim pass, September 6, 2026.

The source says Haloquadratum walsbyi cells 'are arranged in square clusters of four cells'. The primary morphology paper (Bolhuis et al., 'Morphological and Structural Aspects of the Extremely Halophilic Archaeon Haloquadratum walsbyi', PMC3084702) describes flat square cells joined in fragile postage-stamp sheets, not fixed quartets; the genus name refers to the square cell shape. The local page says sheets of square cells with a visible Source note and footer disclosure. Found by the prose claim pass, September 6, 2026.

The prose dates John Snow's water-source cholera study to 1848 while the same module's timeline figure dates it to 1854, the year of the Broad Street and water-company investigations. The page follows the module's own figure, with a visible Source note and footer disclosure. Found by the prose claim pass, September 6, 2026.

The Ions paragraph gives sodium 11 neutrons and chlorine 17 neutrons. Sodium is monoisotopic (sodium-23: 11 protons, 12 neutrons; NIST Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions), and the same module's Atomic Number and Mass paragraph gives chlorine's majority isotope 17 protons and 18 neutrons, so the Ions paragraph contradicts its own section. The local page prints 12 and 18 with a visible Source note and discloses the change in its footer. Found by the prose claim pass sample, September 6, 2026. ALSO (erratum 376): The Carbon Dating box says carbon-14 decays to nitrogen-14 'by a process called beta decay-electrons or positrons emission.' Carbon-14 decays 100% by beta-minus (electron) emission to nitrogen-14 (LNHB Table de Radionucleides; NNDC/ENSDF); positron emission would lower the atomic number, not raise it to nitrogen. The local page says electron emission with a visible Source note and footer disclosure. Found by the prose claim pass sample, September 6, 2026.

The source says Golgi observed the stacked membranes in Plasmodium cells. Golgi's 1898 communication described the internal reticular apparatus in neurons of the cerebellum and spinal ganglia (Bentivoglio et al., Frontiers in Neuroanatomy 13 [2019], doi:10.3389/fnana.2019.00003); his malaria work was separate. The page says nerve cells with a visible Source note and footer disclosure. Found by the prose claim pass, September 6, 2026. ALSO (erratum 381): The source dates de Duve's discovery of lysosomes to the 1960s. The primary paper is de Duve et al., Biochemical Journal 60 (1955): 604-617; the 1960s work was peroxisomes (Bonetta, Journal of Cell Biology 169 [2005]: 705, doi:10.1083/jcb1695fta2). The page says 1955 with a visible Source note and footer disclosure. Found by the prose claim pass, September 6, 2026.

Three source claims fail against the module or independent taxonomy evidence. The Deltaproteobacteria table calls Desulfovibrio 'formerly Desufuromonas'; LPSN identifies Desufuromonas as a misspelling of the separate valid genus Desulfuromonas, not a former name of Desulfovibrio, so the local table omits the parenthetical and places a visible Source note below it. The section summary says nitrogen-fixing Alphaproteobacteria convert atmospheric nitrogen to nitrites, while this book's §§4.1 and 8.7 identify ammonia as the product of nitrogen fixation and reserve nitrite/nitrate production for nitrification; the local summary says ammonia and carries a visible Source note. The Glossary says all Alphaproteobacteria are oligotrophs, while this module's defining paragraph says only some species are; the local definition follows the module and carries a visible Source note. All three corrections are disclosed in the attribution footer.

The cyanobacteria discussion contains two substantive scientific errors. It says nitrogen fixation converts molecular nitrogen to nitrites and nitrates, while this book's §§4.1 and 8.7 identify ammonia as the direct product and nitrification as the later oxidation to nitrite and nitrate. It also calls cyanophycin a secondary photosynthetic pigment alongside phycocyanin; this book's §8.6 lists phycocyanin but not cyanophycin among photosynthetic pigments, and Watzer and Forchhammer (Applied and Environmental Microbiology 84, e01298-18; doi:10.1128/AEM.01298-18) experimentally describe cyanophycin as a carbon/nitrogen storage polymer. The local page corrects both claims, carries a visible Source note beside each, and discloses both in its attribution footer.
